spawn_record_fragments_do_not_carry_the_.what:
OFFLINE, first-hand, second session of 2026-10-12, and it settles the 'check whether our replay actually delivers it' half of the previous session's next step. METHOD: parse the committed replay with the repo's own `azoth_world.javelin.replay_store` + `bundle.decode_bundle` (78 of 79 bundles decode; seq 0x25 is the known datagram-preamble exception), then walk the spawn record's fragments using the live-measured per-fragment byte counts from `.azoth/captures/probes/fragment-bytes.jsonl` - the first 40 of the 48 fragments are therefore known exactly (39413 of 46391 fragment bytes, keys/types reproduced from `fragment-grammar.jsonl`). RESULT 1: the spawn record is re-sent 24 times in the replay (record_id 1 / fragment_count 48 / payload 46393 B, replication seq 1 every time). RESULT 2: the measured live player position (9343.6416, 2786.7327, 87.538) (see `w_does_not_move_the_player_measured_with_the_client_accessor_20261012`) appears NOWHERE in the whole replay - not in the spawn record's 46393 payload bytes and not in any of the 177 messages - in float32, float64, or as int16/int32/int64 fixed point at x1/x10/x100/x1000/x1024/x4096. (Method trap that cost a check: `messages-redacted.txt` is an xxd TEXT dump, so a raw byte search over the file always returns 0; the search must run over the DECODED bodies.) RESULT 3: the player's 16-byte actor id `1a954abc4b3185bfbe37c3d8592618e0` DOES occur exactly once in the spawn payload, at offset 0x7423, inside fragment n=23 key=0 type=10 (40 B body `01 03 a660eeeb eb c75cb7be 6b ab11eb83 17 31 000000 02 <16-byte actor id> 4abb`). So the spawn record does carry the player's identity; it does not carry the player's position. RESULT 4: only 48 of the entity's 126 components have a fragment, so the spawn record is not 'the component list' either. CONSEQUENCE: 'the replay never delivers the position' is now measured, not inferred, and the position work cannot be closed by finding the right fragment in the replay. Note the earlier claim that all fragments carry `type_index` 1 is WRONG: the measured keys/types are 48 distinct keys mapping 1:1 to 47 distinct type indices (only type 1755 is shared, by keys 61 and 76). The captured fragment-type GUIDs are real but unnameable by adjacency (name-before-GUID works for Javelin messages, not for these descriptors), so 1 of 48 has a name (`telemetry`).

CORRECTION 2026-10-18: RESULT 2 above is WRONG as stated. The player position DOES appear in the spawn payload - the 8-byte big-endian f32 PAIR is at payload offset 38332 (9343.6416015625, 2786.732666015625), re-verified with the repo's own decode_bundle. The original search looked for the 12-byte TRIPLE including z=87.538, and z is not on the wire in any encoding (which is the separate, correct finding that the wire carries a 2D position and the client derives the height). Searching for the pair succeeds; searching for the triple cannot. The 2026-10-14 result `server_owns_the_player_position_measured_20261014` (0.0000 u error against the client's own accessor) is the one to trust.

NEW VERIFICATION STEP (use this before blaming the client): the world server logs its EFFECTIVE config as its first log line, `{"event":"config","replay_local_player_uuid":...,"input_response":...,"chunk_gap_ms":...}`. config_event_is_the_effective_config_202.what: DIAGNOSTIC, first-hand, 2026-10-12. The world server writes its EFFECTIVE runtime configuration as the first event of every session: 28 fields including `replay_local_player_uuid`, `replay_local_player_uuid_seqs`, `replay_split_seq`, `replay_split_delay_s`, `chunk_gap_ms`, `heartbeat`, `input_response`, `position_reply`, `position_reply_target`, `start_movement`, `state_stream`, `activity_stream`, `channel1_echo`, `replay_enabled`, `replay_max_seq`. WHY IT MATTERS: the world is started by `python az.py dev`, which forwards whatever `AZOTH_*` variables the CALLING shell happens to have; a variable set in another shell is not forwarded (AGENTS.md already warns about this for AZOTH_LOG_RAW). That makes 'which experiment did I actually run?' easy to get wrong, and TWO of this session's own conclusions were wrong until this line was read - first because the wrong config was read from an accumulated 12-session log, then because the Frida crash below was blamed on the exit timer. There is one `config` event per session, so an accumulated `world.log` needs the LAST one (or a split on `listening-dtls`), not the first. TOOL NOTE: `.azoth/logs/world.log` holds every session ever run (671k lines / 264 MB here; it grew to 2.6 GB in services/world/rep_traffic.jsonl before). Split on `listening-dtls` or delete before measuring. TRAP FOUND WHILE USING IT (2026-10-12, and it nearly produced a false protocol claim): the `outbound-app-data` event's `records[].channel` histogram does NOT cover every server send. On a measured session it reported only channels 0 and 3 while the same session logged 376 `input-response` events, and the input responses are documented to go out on channel 1 (see the `AZOTH_REPLAY_INPUT_RESPONSE` lever). So 'the server never sends on channel 1', read off that histogram, is a LOGGING GAP, not a protocol fact. Count the purpose-specific events (`input-response`, `position-reply`, `heartbeat`, `keepalive`) separately from `outbound-app-data` before making any claim about which channels the server uses.

frida_agent_unload_crash_reproduced_2026.what: REPRODUCTION, 2026-10-12, second independent instance. The existing record `frida_agent_unload_is_a_crash_source_20261012` had ONE instance (run comp-083309) and the handoff had to hedge it as 'correlation, not proof'. A second, differently-written probe produced the identical signature: WER `Fault bucket 1667254714238955796, type 5, Event Name: BEX64`, `P1: NewWorld.exe`, `P4: frida-agent.dll_unloaded`, `P6: 6ac0026b`, `P7: 000000000009c7e0`, `P8: c0000005`. SAME module, SAME offset 0x9c7e0. WHAT HAPPENED: `reverse/probes/client/frida-facet-slots.py` (new, this session) attached at 18:24:20Z, found no live entity because it was attached AFTER the world had loaded (the local-player entity is only observable during the load - see `player_entity_component_list_measured_20261012`), timed out at 150 s, detached at ~18:26:50Z, and the client died at 18:27:13. Game.log ends at 18:26:50.754 with a routine CMS heartbeat - no `Cleanup()`, no `exiting to main menu`, no `Disconnected from REP`, no `transportError` - i.e. a SILENT death with no client-side log line, which is why it initially looked like the exit timer. THE METHOD RULE THIS PRODUCES: (1) the faulting module in the WER event is the first thing to read before interpreting a session death, because the client logs nothing when its own agent is unloaded; (2) a Frida probe that DETACHES can kill the process, so detach is not a safe way to end an experiment - treat 'attach, measure, detach' as a potentially fatal sequence and either keep the probe attached, end the client deliberately, or accept that the session is spent; (3) any session in which a Frida agent was attached and then unloaded has an alternative explanation for its death and must say so. HOW TO READ THE EVENT: `Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Application'; Id=1001; StartTime=(Get-Date).AddMinutes(-20)}` and read P4/P7/P8. `Report.wer` under C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\WER\ReportArchive is ACL-restricted and cannot be read as a normal user - the event message carries the same signature fields.

client_facets_ARE_bound_on_the_live_play.what: MEASURED LIVE 2026-10-12 (second session), and it CORRECTS the framing of `position_facets_absent_on_the_live_entity_20261012`. Client facets ARE created for the local player. Where a facet lives: NOT as a member of the entity's component list, but at `component + 0x80` on its owning component (the factories store it there: `lVar = RuntimeClassRegistry::CreateByName(registry, name, size, align); <owner> + 0x80 = ctor(lVar); <facet> + 8 = <owner>` - see `client_facet_creation_is_a_by_name_factory_20261012`). Measured on the live entity, 126 components, all resolved, by reading `[component + 0x80]` and then reading the candidate's own vtable slot 0 for its AZ type GUID: **110 of 126 components have a bound facet object**, 108 distinct facet GUIDs, 106 of them named in the AZ registry, and **106 of 106 named ones end in `*ClientFacet`** - i.e. the binding is exactly the client-facet family, with zero exceptions. The 16 without a facet are `TagComponent`, `PlayerSaveData`, `TriggerAreaDetectable`, `FootstepComponent`, `SkinnedMeshComponent`, `MotionParameterSmoothingComponent`, one unnamed type, and EIGHT audio/vegetation components (`AudioProxyComponent`, `AudioPreloadComponent`, `AudioTriggerComponent`, `AudioRtpcComponent`, `AudioDataFollowerComponent`, `AudioEnvironmentComponent`, `VegetationBendingComponent`, `VegetationAudioComponent`) - **none of them is a position component**. THE SPECIFIC CORRECTION: `PlayerPositionTrackingComponent` (index 95, GUID 62620B33-6F37-418B-9C4F-62AD6058D54D) IS on the entity **and its `PlayerPositionTrackingComponentClientFacet` (B74D06BC-123E-4C39-A842-EB8CDE4B6DAF) IS BOUND at +0x80** - the exact class the previous entry recorded as absent. `CameraLockComponent` also has its facet bound. WHY THE PREVIOUS ENTRY GOT IT WRONG: it searched the ENTITY'S COMPONENT LIST for names like `PlayerPositionTrackingComponentClientFacet` and `IPositionReceiver`. A facet is not a component of the entity, so that search cannot succeed, and an INTERFACE is not a component either, so its absence from a component list is not evidence about it. The entry conflated three different kinds of object - (a) components of the entity, (b) client facets bound to components, (c) interfaces a facet may implement - and its conclusion 'the client-side facets are not created on the local player entity' is FALSE as stated. WHAT SURVIVES FROM IT, restated: of the position family, only `PlayerPositionTrackingComponent` is a COMPONENT of this entity; `PositionInTheWorldComponent`, `PositionalTicketingComponent` and `CameraComponent` are not components of it at all (so the replicated-state facet `PositionInTheWorldComponentServerFacet::InitializeReplicatedFields` has no local carrier here). That is a statement about which COMPONENTS the entity has, not about facet creation, and it is the remaining lead. ALSO MEASURED: there is no `GlobalStorage`/`Storage` component on the entity either - so the 23 unbound `GlobalStorageComponentClientFacet_ReceiveStorageSearchItems` errors are the same shape of mistake (a class absent from THIS entity, not a broken facet mechanism). CONSEQUENCE FOR THE MOVEMENT WORK: stop treating 'the client-side facets are not created' as the blocker; the facet machinery demonstrably works for the local player, including for the position component that is present. The open question is what the position component's facet does with the input stream and why the authoritative position never arrives - i.e. back to the replicated-state path, not to facet creation.

frida_unload_crash_mechanism_and_the_fix.va: frida-agent.dll RVA 0x9c7e0 (function 0x9c7e0..0x9cbd7, 1015 bytes, per its .pdata RUNTIME_FUNCTION); WER event 1001 'BEX64'
frida_unload_crash_mechanism_and_the_fix.what: ROOT CAUSE AND A WORKING FIX, 2026-10-12, first-hand, and this replaces the 'correlation, not proof' framing. THE MECHANISM. Windows reports the crash as `Event Name: BEX64`, `P4: frida-agent.dll_unloaded`, `P7: 000000000009c7e0`, `P8: c0000005`, and - the field that identifies it - **`P9: 0000000000000008`**, which is an EXECUTE violation (DEP), not a read or write. Disassembling `frida-agent.dll` at that offset (the DLL is on disk for every attach, under `.azoth/tmp/frida-<hash>/x86_64/frida-agent.dll`; the hashes present matched the probe times exactly) shows `0x9c7e0` is the **first instruction of a function** (`mov rax, rsp` of a large prologue), and `.pdata` confirms the range `0x9c7e0..0x9cbd7`. So a thread took a branch to a function ENTRY inside a module that had already been unmapped: a textbook execute-after-unload race, i.e. the agent was unloaded while client threads could still be routed into it. The client logs NOTHING for this - no `Cleanup()`, no `exiting to main menu`, no `Disconnected from REP`, Game.log simply stops mid-heartbeat - which is why three earlier readings of it went wrong (it looked like the 20-minute timer). WHY DETACH IS THE WRONG ENDING. A bare `session.detach()` unloads the agent while the hooks installed by the script may still be reachable, so any client thread that reaches a hooked prologue after unload branches into freed memory. Measured three times on one day (two different probes), each time 20-25 s after the Python side ended the session. THE FIX, VERIFIED. `reverse/probes/client/_paths.py::safe_shutdown()` now offers two strategies: (1) `kill=True` - `device.kill(pid)`, which ends the client deliberately, so there is no unload and no race at all (usually correct here, because every world A/B already needs a fresh `NewWorld.exe`); (2) `kill=False` - the orderly sequence `Interceptor.detachAll()` in the agent, settle, `script.unload()`, settle, `session.detach()`, which removes the hook routing BEFORE the module can go away. **Measured result for strategy (2), and its LIMIT.** Two orderly teardowns (19:17Z and ~19:20Z) were followed by a live client - checked at 19:18:19 and 19:20:38 - against three same-day crashes at ~23 s with a bare detach, so the frida-agent BEX64 signature did **not** recur. **But the client still died ~7 minutes after spawn (19:22:16Z), and the WER event says it was a DIFFERENT failure:** `Event Name: APPCRASH`, `P4: ntdll.dll`, `P7: c0000005`, `P8: 0x165497`, `P9` empty (a read/write violation, not an execute one). That is the same family as the `ntdll.dll` crashes already on record (`0x1662b7` three times, `0xc4a0f`), and it is 0x165497, a new offset. So: the orderly teardown removes THIS crash source and is not a session fix; the actual long-session blocker remains the ntdll access violation, and a session in which probes were attached and detached now has to be split into 'agent-unload crash' (fixed) and 'ntdll crash' (open) before it is interpreted. Probes that hook a hot function now export `teardown()` (`Interceptor.detachAll()`) and take a `--shutdown kill|detach` flag. Frida 17's `Session` has no `.device` attribute, so the device must be passed in from the attach call. WHAT IS STILL UNEXPLAINED: why the unload is reached at all when nothing should be executing agent code (every hook payload here is small) - the pattern worth acting on is that the two probes that crashed both hook the hot component lookup `FUN_1413fb700`, while the light position probe did not die.

The HUD cable verdict is computed in one place and the comparison is exactly: `now = FUN_141413890(); age = now - *(u64*)(hud + 0xAA8); if (age > red_threshold) state = 2; else state = (age > amber_threshold); FUN_1433d4660(0xc1fd05e0, &state, 1);` - so `state` is 0 (clear), 1 (amber) or 2 (red), and the two thresholds are client cvars read through `_DAT_149f20f90`/`_DAT_149f21048`. WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE OPEN BLOCKER: if nothing refreshes `hud+0xAA8`, `age` grows monotonically and the icon walks clear -> amber -> red on its own, which is exactly the sequence the user reports. The previous live finding that the stamp 'moved once (at replay-complete-quiet) then froze' (`alc_pointer_never_opens_live_20261011`) is therefore the whole story so far: the stamp is written at least once and then not refreshed. THE HUD OBJECT IS NOT THE CONNECTION OBJECT: in this function `param_1` also carries fields at +0x421, +0x1190, +0x1622, +0x1690, so it is the large HUD/game object, not a small connection object. WHY THE WRITER WAS NEVER FOUND, AND THE TRAP FOR THE NEXT ATTEMPT: `+0xAA8` is NOT unique to that class. A displacement search over the image (writes only) finds 42 instructions in 42 distinct functions touching `[reg+0xAA8]`, plus 68 `lea` sites computing an address with that displacement, and several of those writers are the SAME constructor pattern (`lea rax,[rip+const]; mov qword [rdi+0xAA8], rax`) initialising a POINTER field in unrelated classes. A displacement-based search or a Frida hook on the raw offset therefore catches unrelated classes and cannot identify the ALC field. The correct next step is to identify the CLASS of the HUD object from the HUD function's callers (`FUN_14486c740` has exactly 2: 0x14485d663 and 0x14485e6c7) and hook that class's specific writer, not the offset. The ALC replicated state has a small family of helpers, all keyed off the singleton global _DAT_14a33d3d8 (which holds the state registry at +0x30): `FUN_142a3d460` registers the type - it builds a descriptor `{0x8000, 0x1570, 0x1570, ...}` and calls FUN_1413da9f0(registry+0x48, &desc), where **0x1570 == 0x1560 + 0x10**, i.e. the object size plus its alignment, so the state is registered with a 0x1560-byte footprint; `FUN_142a43b30` is the allocate-N helper and calls the registry's allocator as `(registry+0x30 -> vtable[0x10])(reg, param_2, param_3 * 0x1560, 0x10)`, i.e. it allocates an ARRAY of ALCReplicatedState at 0x1560 bytes per element; and `FUN_142a3b050` is the single-object allocator (CreateByName by name 0x1480fed90). So the engine supports MULTIPLE ALCReplicatedState instances - one per actor whose ALC state is tracked - which is consistent with the registry walk showing four `TimeComponentClientFacet` instances and is a reason the local player's own state cannot be assumed to be 'the' ALC state. TOOL NOTE (and a corrected negative): the first attempt to find these users was a whole-.text linear Capstone sweep, which reported **0** references to the `ALCReplicatedState` name even though `FUN_142a3b050` plainly contains `142a3b117 lea rdx,[rip+0x56c3c72]` -> `0x1480fed90`. A linear sweep over 132 MB desynchronises on data and one bad byte silently swallows every later reference, making the result look like a confident negative. New tool `reverse/tools/find-rip-lea.py` matches the RIP-relative LEA opcode pattern instead (48/4C 8D with modrm.rm=101), so it cannot desync, and it reproduces the by-hand result. It found the complete reference sets: the name is used by 0x142a3b117 and 0x142a3c270; the allocator's field table by 0x142a3b086, 0x142a3d4a9 (inside FUN_142a3d460) and 0x142a43b56 (inside FUN_142a43b30); `ALCLocalClient` by exactly one site, 0x14486d833 inside FUN_14486c740. NEXT STEP: the record id / trait that carries this state is declared by `ActionListComponentServerFacet::InitializeReplicatedFields` (its lambda type descriptor is at file offset 0xa224c93); that function is the place to find which record id the client's handler table uses for ALC state.

in_game_state_machine_does_not_mean_the_.va: client Game.log: `[WARNING] Slice:` lines vs `player spawn succeeds` / `Update state ... InGame`; scripts/private-run.py verdict()
in_game_state_machine_does_not_mean_the_.what: MEASURED, 2026-10-13, and it is an instrument defect that produced false positives in this project for days. `scripts/private-run.py` reported `verdict: InGame reached, player possessed` on the strength of the client's state machine, and a session that is HUNG ON A LOADING SCREEN satisfies that: the client logs `player spawn succeeds, in game` and `Update state WaitingForPlayerSpawn to new state InGame` and then sits on a loading screen showing '(Not Responding)'. Two sessions on the same build, compared: the hung one (ch1 server-container, 17:44Z) had **5** post-spawn non-boilerplate log lines and **0** `[WARNING] Slice:` lines; the session that genuinely rendered the world (19:11Z) had **35** such lines and **26** `[WARNING] Slice:`. `[WARNING] Slice:` is emitted only while streaming world slices, so it is a mechanical 'did the world actually load' signal. FIXED in the runner: it now waits up to `--render-timeout` (default 90 s) after the spawn marker for the first Slice line, reports the count in the verdict, and **exits 1** with an explicit verdict when the state machine says InGame but zero slices were seen. CONSEQUENCE FOR EARLIER RECORDS: any session reported as 'InGame reached, player possessed' without this check may have been a hung loading screen, and the one that stayed alive ~60 minutes while apparently in-world was one of them - the network stack and the server kept running normally while the client was frozen, which is why it was easy to misread. The 'did it render' signal to use from now on is the Slice count, not the state machine.

red_cable_reproduced_on_a_rendered_sessi.va: scripts/watch-indicator.py classify() against the game client crop; game client rect (277,167)-(1643,935)
red_cable_reproduced_on_a_rendered_sessi.what: MEASURED, 2026-10-13, and this is the valid baseline the cable A/B needed. On a session whose world was genuinely rendered (26 `[WARNING] Slice:` lines, state machine to InGame, 0 timeouts), the indicator read **RED (disconnected)**, red 3.66%, yellow 1.77%, with the screenshot kept (research/sessions/session-20261013T1911Z-baseline-rendered/hud-red-cable.png shows the unplugged-cable icon with its warning triangle). TWO MEASUREMENT TRAPS recorded because both produced false readings first: (1) a desktop capture contains the T3 window AND the game window, so classifying the whole desktop against the documented box (34,350,130,470) samples the wrong pixels and returns `absent/other`; the box is in the GAME CLIENT's own pixel space, so a desktop capture must first be cropped to the window's client rect (`GetClientRect` + `ClientToScreen`); (2) a LOADING SCREEN does not draw the HUD cable at all, so any cable reading taken while the client is still loading is meaningless regardless of how the box is computed - check the Slice count first (see `in_game_state_machine_does_not_mean_the_world_rendered_20261013`). TWO OFFERED EXPLANATIONS FOR THE RED CABLE THAT THIS SESSION RULED OUT, both by measurement rather than argument: the ALC reply IS delivered continuously (414 input-response events, 828 messages) and the cable still goes red (see `alc_reply_is_delivered_and_the_cable_still_goes_red_20261013`), and the state stream does not clear it either (see `state_stream_does_not_clear_the_cable_or_move_the_player_20261012`). So the cable's cause is still open, but the candidate space is now: the stamp on the ALC local client is not refreshed by anything we currently send, and the ALC replicated state (`MB::ALCReplicatedState`, whose replicated fields include worldPosRel/worldPosAbs) is the most likely thing that would refresh it.

RED_CABLE_FIXED_record1_state_stream_ref.va: ALC local client +0xAA8 (age read by FUN_14486c740, printed by FUN_14487b300); refresher = the local player's own AOI state record (record_id 1); lever AZOTH_REPLAY_STATE_STREAM_ONLY_RECORD in services/world/src/azoth_world/rep.py
RED_CABLE_FIXED_record1_state_stream_ref.what: RESOLVED, 2026-10-13, MEASURED BOTH WAYS. The red HUD cable is a pure client-side age of the ALC local client's `+0xAA8` stamp (`age = FUN_141413890() - *(alc+0xAA8)`; amber ~2 s, red ~15 s; the same field is printed by the debug overlay as 'Time since last response: %s'), and **nothing the server was sending refreshed it**. WHAT REFRESHES IT: the local player's own AOI state record. In the capture that is `record_id 1` (the client logs 'Received new local player metadata' for it) and it appears ONLY in the four 7154-byte bundles at replay seq 0x98/0x9A/0x9C/0x9E. Those sit BELOW the state stream's default floor of 0xA0, so the stream never re-sent them; every bundle at or above 0xA0 carries a DIFFERENT record id and does NOT refresh the stamp. MEASUREMENT (new probe reverse/probes/client/frida-alc-stamp.py, which learns the ALC object from its own per-frame update and logs every change of +0xAA8): baseline = **1 change in 140 s, age growing to 262 000 ms** (cable RED); stream from 0xA0 = **1 change, 250 000 ms**; stream from 0x94 (includes the record-1 bundles) = **12 changes, max age ~100 ms** (cable YELLOW); stream restricted to record 1 at 4/s = **225 changes, max age 100 ms** and the indicator box contains **no cable icon at all**. The correlation that pinned it: spawn at 20:11:57.266, stamp set at 20:12:04.538 (7.3 s later, during the replay), `replay-complete-quiet` at 20:12:05, and the stamp never moved again for the rest of the session. THE FIX is configuration plus one small code change: `AZOTH_REPLAY_STATE_STREAM=1`, `_SEQ=1`, `_MIN_SEQ=0x94`, `_ONLY_RECORD=1`, `_PERIOD_S=0.25`, on top of the mandatory `AZOTH_REPLAY_LOCAL_PLAYER_UUID=character`, `AZOTH_REPLAY_INPUT_RESPONSE=1`, `AZOTH_RESEND_INTERVAL_S=1.0`. The code change is `STATE_STREAM_ONLY_RECORD`, which filters the stream to bundles whose FIRST record id matches, so every send is a refresh instead of one in 29. The stream's own arming event proves it: `{"count": 4, "seqs": ["0x98","0x9a","0x9c","0x9e"], "only_record": 1, "period_s": 0.25, "loop": true}`. TWO CANDIDATES RULED OUT BY MEASUREMENT ALONG THE WAY: the `0x1096`/`0x1097` input response (delivered 414 times / 828 messages, stamp still frozen) and the state stream at its default floor (sent continuously, stamp still frozen). CAVEAT FOR THE NEXT READER: the fixed run's indicator box reads 'YELLOW 11.48%' from the classifier, but looking at the crop shows only wall - the icon is ABSENT. The classifier's amber rule matches the wall's gold pixels, so the label must not be quoted without the image.

local_player_state_record_is_record_id_1.va: record_id 1 of the type-0x08 state bundle; capture seq 0x98/0x9A/0x9C/0x9E (7154 bytes each)
local_player_state_record_is_record_id_1.what: STATIC + MEASURED, 2026-10-13. The local player's own AOI state is carried by `record_id 1`, and in the committed capture it appears in exactly four bundles - replay seq 0x98, 0x9A, 0x9C, 0x9E, each 7154 bytes with `record_id 1 / fragment_count 9`. Decoding them gives `[00 01 08][8-byte prologue][varint payload length]` then records `[u8 record_id][u8 fragment_count][fragments...]`. WHY THIS MATTERED: the state stream's default `AZOTH_REPLAY_STATE_STREAM_MIN_SEQ=0xA0` selects bundles 0xA0..0xB0, whose record ids are 22, 29, 10, 30, 60, 79, 87, 44, 88, 58, 89, 72, 90, 35, 91, 92, 70 - i.e. the stream was re-sending everybody ELSE's state and never the local player's. That is why streaming appeared to do nothing for both open symptoms: the record that would refresh the ALC stamp (and, plausibly, that would carry the player's own position) was never in the stream. The local player's actor id appears in the spawn record (record 1, 48 fragments) but NOT in any of the 0xA0..0xB0 bundles, which is the earlier measured reason the stream could not deliver the player's position either. Generalisation to check next: whether record_id 1 is also what carries the replicated position for the local player - the ALC state's replicated field list includes worldPosRel/worldPosAbs, and record 1 is the local-player slot, so the two questions are likely the same one.

local_player_position_is_no_longer_froze.va: record_id 1 state bundles (capture seq 0x98/0x9A/0x9C/0x9E) sent 4/s; position read via FUN_140fddfa0
local_player_position_is_no_longer_froze.what: MEASURED LIVE, 2026-10-13, and it is the FIRST time any server-sent data has changed the local player's position. Before this, every measured session had the position frozen at exactly (9343.6416, 2786.7327, 87.538) - 667/667 identical samples in one window, and unchanged through W and S holds in several sessions. With the record-1 state stream active (see `RED_CABLE_FIXED_record1_state_stream_refreshes_the_alc_stamp_20261013`) the position is different and it MOVES: first sample (9354.0039, 2766.1936, 87.5475), 50 distinct values in a monotonic drift, settling at (9354.3965, 2766.3806, 87.5629). So the client now APPLIES the local player's replicated state, which is the mechanism by which the server can move the player at all. HONEST CONTROL, same run, position sampled at 0.2 s: with NO input over 10 s the delta was [0.0,0.0,0.0] (it had already settled) and with **W held for 10 s** the delta was also [0.0,0.0,0.0]. MOVEMENT IS NOT SOLVED: the drift was a one-time convergence onto the state being sent, after which the player is static and W has no effect. Note also that neither the settled value (9354.3965, 2766.3806) nor the previously frozen (9343.6416, 2786.7327) appears anywhere in the replay's 177 messages, so the position the client converged to is not simply a captured byte string being copied. NEXT EXPERIMENT (the one this makes possible): take a record-1 bundle, modify its position field, and send it - if the player goes there, the server becomes authoritative over the position, which is the movement gate.

MOVEMENT_WORKS_state_stream_enables_play.va: state stream of captured type-0x08 bundles (services/world/src/azoth_world/rep.py, AZOTH_REPLAY_STATE_STREAM, defaults now ON / MIN_SEQ 0x94 / period 1 s + player record 1 at 4 Hz); position read with FUN_140fddfa0
MOVEMENT_WORKS_state_stream_enables_play.what: RESOLVED AND CAUSALLY ATTRIBUTED, 2026-10-13. **The player moves.** For the whole history of this project the local position was frozen at exactly (9343.6416, 2786.7327, 87.538) and W did nothing - 667/667 identical samples in the most thorough earlier measurement. It moves now, and one variable explains both that and the red cable. EVIDENCE, three runs with the same mandatory env (AZOTH_REPLAY_LOCAL_PLAYER_UUID=character, AZOTH_REPLAY_INPUT_RESPONSE=1, AZOTH_RESEND_INTERVAL_S=1.0) and the position sampled at 0.2 s with the client's own accessor: (1) **repro run, state stream ON (defaults)**: no input for 5 s gave 2 samples, net 0.0 u (STILL); then W held 10 s gave 55 samples, **53 distinct positions, net displacement 20.784 u** ((9344.6123,2784.7363,87.5667) -> (9353.9258,2766.1565,87.5442)). (2) **first run, state stream ON**: W held ~12 s gave 92 distinct positions and **83.026 u** of net displacement, while the pre-W phase was frozen at 0.0. The two runs move in DIFFERENT world directions ((-10.3,+82.4) vs (+9.3,-18.6)), which is what WASD-relative forward looks like when the character faces a different way, and is evidence the motion is the player's own movement rather than one canned displacement. (3) **A/B, state stream OFF, one variable**: 5 samples, **1 distinct position**, exactly (9343.6416, 2786.7327, 87.538) - the same frozen constant as every previous session - and W moved nothing. THE MECHANISM: the client only simulates the local player when it is receiving the player's own AOI state. Our server replayed the capture once and then stopped; the state stream resumes it, but with the old floor of 0xA0 it re-sent only OTHER entities' records (0xA0..0xB0 carry record ids 22,29,10,30,60,79,87,44,88,58,89,72,90,35,91,92,70) and never record id 1, which is the local player. The floor is now 0x94 so the four record-1 bundles (seq 0x98/0x9A/0x9C/0x9E) are included, and they are additionally re-sent at 4 Hz so the ALC stamp stays young (see RED_CABLE_FIXED_record1_state_stream_refreshes_the_alc_stamp_20261013). So the SAME missing record explains both open symptoms: the client never received the player's own state, so it never simulated the player (no movement) and its ALC 'last response' stamp aged out (red cable). IN THE SAME A/B RUN the cable was also measured: stream OFF -> **RED (disconnected, red 3.7%)**; stream ON -> the indicator box contains NO icon at all. BOTH ACCEPTANCE GATES ARE NOW MET as measured: the local transform changes while W is held and is still when no input is given, and the HUD cable clears - each with a one-variable control.

state_stream_defaults_are_the_fix_not_an.va: services/world/src/azoth_world/rep.py: STATE_STREAM_ENABLED (default 1), STATE_STREAM_PERIOD_S (1.0), STATE_STREAM_MIN_SEQ (0x94), STATE_STREAM_PLAYER_RECORD (1), STATE_STREAM_PLAYER_PERIOD_S (0.25), STATE_STREAM_REWRITE_SEQ (default 1), STATE_STREAM_ONLY_RECORD (-1 = no filter)
state_stream_defaults_are_the_fix_not_an.what: CODE CHANGE, 2026-10-13, turning the state stream from an opt-in experiment into the correct default. The stream was previously OFF by default because an earlier version broke the connection (2026-10-04: REP dropped 23 s after spawn, the client reconnected and never re-created its ClientContext). That breakage was the replication-counter rewrite writing ONE RAW BYTE, which widens a one-byte varint into two and shifts every fragment; the rewrite now re-encodes through the verified parser (`javelin.bundle.with_replication_seq`) and is safe, so the stream is what makes the session correct and OFF is the broken configuration. Defaults now encode two measurements: the floor reaches the local player's bundles (0x94 rather than 0xA0, because record 1 lives only at 0x98/0x9A/0x9C/0x9E), and the player's record gets its own 4 Hz timer while the rest of the world state keeps ~1/s, because the cable only clears when the ALC stamp is refreshed faster than its ~2 s amber threshold. THE BUG FOUND WHILE SETTING THESE DEFAULTS, and it is the failure mode this project keeps hitting: `AZOTH_REPLAY_STATE_STREAM_ONLY_RECORD` was written as an EQUALITY against its own sentinel, so the default -1 matched no bundle. The stream armed with `count: 0` while the config event still reported `state_stream: True` and the arming event looked entirely normal - a silent no-op that left the cable RED with nothing in any log to explain it. It is now `_state_stream_selected()` (negative = no filter) with a test, and the arming event logs `count`, `seqs`, `player_bundles` and the periods so an empty arm is visible. RULE: a lever that arms with nothing must say so; add the count to the arming event of every stream.
state_stream_defaults_are_the_fix_not_an.found_by: live 2026-10-13; the `state-stream-armed` event reported `count: 0` on a run whose cable was RED, leading to the equality-vs-sentinel bug; fixed with a regression test (test_negative_only_record_means_no_filter)

WASD_verified_all_four_directions_202610.va: FUN_140fddfa0 position accessor, sampled at 0.2 s with a wall-clock stamp per sample; keys sent as real scan codes (W=0x11, S=0x1F, A=0x1E, D=0x20)
WASD_verified_all_four_directions_202610.what: MEASURED AND VERIFIED, 2026-10-13. All four movement keys move the player, in the correct directions, and the player stops when they are released. Env: the mandatory three only (`AZOTH_REPLAY_LOCAL_PLAYER_UUID=character`, `AZOTH_REPLAY_INPUT_RESPONSE=1`, `AZOTH_RESEND_INTERVAL_S=1.0`); the state stream is ON by default and needs no variables. Per-phase results (each key held 5 s, position sampled at 0.2 s, phases bounded by recorded wall-clock markers): baseline no input **0.000 u** net over 28 samples; W **22.998 u** in (+10.079,-20.672); S **18.975 u** in (-8.341,+17.043); A **4.515 u** in (+4.018,+2.060); D **9.359 u** in (-8.212,-4.488); after release **0.003 u**. DIRECTION ANALYSIS: W vs S = **179.9 deg** (opposite), A vs D = **178.5 deg** (opposite), W vs A = **91.2 deg** (perpendicular), W vs D = **87.3 deg** (perpendicular), and the vertical drift across all four phases stays within 0.16 u over ~23 u of horizontal travel. Three further properties rule out a canned or random displacement: the per-phase PATH length equals the NET displacement (23.039 vs 22.998, 18.980 vs 18.975), i.e. straight-line motion with no jitter or rubber-banding; the two opposing keys are near-exactly anti-parallel; and the perpendicular pair is near-exactly orthogonal to forward. The player is also still when no input is given and stops again within 2 s of the last release, which is the second half of the movement acceptance criterion. See `MOVEMENT_WORKS_state_stream_enables_player_simulation_20261013` for the one-variable A/B that attributes all of this to the local player's own state record being streamed. CAVEAT: verified over 5 s windows in a session that ran ~22 min; a 30-minute proof and a 2-hour soak are still outstanding, and soak runs must be probe-free because a measurement probe caused the last client crash.

session_still_crashes_and_the_cable_clas.va: WER Application event 1001: APPCRASH, P4 StackHash_2264, P7 c0000005, P8 PCH_0E_FROM_unknown+0x0; scripts/watch-indicator.py + scripts/measure-cable.py
session_still_crashes_and_the_cable_clas.what: TWO HONEST LIMITATIONS, measured 2026-10-13 on the same run, recorded because both would otherwise be quoted as successes. (1) THE SESSION STILL CRASHES, and not from Frida this time. Run 2026-10-13T22:07Z: spawn 22:07:17, client dead at 22:19:01 - about **11 min 44 s** - with `Event Name: APPCRASH`, `P4: StackHash_2264`, `P7: c0000005`, `P8: PCH_0E_FROM_unknown+0x0000000000000000`. A StackHash signature means the faulting address was not inside any loaded module, which is what stack corruption or a corrupted return address looks like - a DIFFERENT failure from the frida-agent unload crashes (`frida-agent.dll` + `0x9c7e0`/`0x9c7f4`) and from the ntdll ones (`0x1662b7`, `0x165497`). NO probe was attached at the time: the light position probe used earlier in the run had already exited. Game.log simply stops at a routine CMS heartbeat 37 s before the crash, with `exiting to main menu` 0, `Cleanup()` 0, `Disconnected from REP` 0, `transportError` 0. So duration is NOT solved: sessions still end in ~12-22 minutes, by at least three distinct crash signatures, and the 30-minute proof and 2-hour soak remain outstanding. NEW HYPOTHESIS worth testing, because the stream is now the busiest thing we do: 284 `state-stream` events per minute (4 record-1 bundles/s, each 7167 bytes and therefore chunked, plus 1 world bundle/s) means the client re-applies the same captured state thousands of times per session, and a client-side bug in repeated re-application would look exactly like this. The test is one variable: raise `AZOTH_REPLAY_STATE_STREAM_PLAYER_PERIOD_S` from 0.25 to ~1.0 (still under the cable's ~2 s amber threshold) and see whether the session lives longer. (2) THE CABLE CLASSIFIER HAS A RED-BACKGROUND FALSE POSITIVE. The soak's first sample at 22:17:40Z reported `RED (disconnected), red 1.8%`, which would read as the cable returning; the saved crop shows an NPC standing in front of a **red curtain** and contains NO icon at all. So the cable was still clear and the verdict was wrong. This is the SECOND false-positive mode found in one day - the first was the amber rule matching Aeternum's gold walls (a crop with no icon read `YELLOW 11.48%`). CONSEQUENCE FOR HOW TO QUOTE THE CABLE: neither colour rule is validated against a real amber sample, and both match ordinary scenery, so a `RED`/`YELLOW` label from `measure-cable.py` is a SCREEN, not a measurement - it is only trustworthy together with its crop. The direct measurement is the ALC stamp age via `frida-alc-stamp.py` (young age = cable clear), which does not depend on scenery at all. CALIBRATION DONE (same day, after that finding). The red rule is now `r >= 180 and g >= 80 and (r-g) >= 90 and abs(g-b) <= 40`, calibrated on one sample of each kind: the real icon's red is a BRIGHT PINK - (225,109,102) and (188,82,73) - while the curtain's is a DULL red (132,65,37), so `r >= 180` alone separates them. The amber threshold was raised to 2.0 % because the curtain's brighter parts tripped the old 0.6 % at 0.62 %. VERIFIED against six known crops: the real red icon reads RED (red 1.44 %, yellow 0.08 %) and the red curtain plus four clean crops all read absent/other (red 0.00 %; yellow 0.00-0.62 %). AMBER REMAINS UNVALIDATED - there is no capture of a real amber cable, so that branch is a guess and its verdict string says so (`YELLOW (warning, UNVALIDATED rule - check the crop)`). A test of the obvious alternative discriminator failed and is recorded so nobody retries it: the icon sits on a near-black plaque, but the box's dark-pixel fraction is 46.0 % for the real icon vs 47.2 % for the curtain, so darkness does not separate them.

client_asks_43_request_types_and_the_ser.va: scripts/inbound-inventory.py against .azoth/logs/world.log; the server-side log of each distinct request is `event: inbound-typed` (rep.py::_note_inbound_typed)
client_asks_43_request_types_and_the_ser.what: MEASURED, 2026-10-13, and it is the answer to 'does our server have everything the client expects?' in the inbound direction. In one session the client sent **43 distinct typed request types**; the server has **no inbound typed-message dispatcher at all** (`grep -c dispatch_inbound` -> 0), so every request is acknowledged at the transport level and then ignored at the application level, with nothing in any log saying so. unrequested_client_facet_responses_were_.what: MEASURED AND FIXED, 2026-10-13. A clean session logged **29** `RMIDispatch: The facet target ID couldn't be found` errors, ALL of them inside a single millisecond and **1 ms BEFORE `player spawn succeeds`**, while the replay drains **8 s AFTER** it. The cause is structural: our replay is another client's capture, so it contains the server's answers to requests our client never makes, and it blasts them at a client whose object graph does not exist yet - and because each message is sent once, that data is lost for the session. WHICH ACTION IS RIGHT depends on whether the client has the facet at all, measured against the live entity's 107 bound client facets: **absent -> drop** (GlobalStorageComponentClientFacet, EventNotificationComponentClientFacet, VoiceChatComponentClientFacet) and **present but not yet built -> defer until the replay drains** (TimeComponentClientFacet, GameModeParticipantComponentClientFacet, GridTrackingComponentClientFacet, ContractsComponentClientFacet). Dropping is not data loss: those answer requests our client never sends - the request behind the 23 storage-search replies is wire 7039 `RequestReplicateStorageSearchResults`, which is not among the client's 43. ACCEPTANCE MEASURED: dispatch errors per session went **29 -> 3 -> 1**. The first drop came from discarding the 25 unreceivable messages (arming event `replay-response-scheduling`: `dropped_unreceivable: 25`, `dropped_types: [0x1067, 0x1b88, 0xca4]`). The next two came from making the input-response lever wait for the client's object graph: it is a CLIENT-FACET RMI and shared one readiness predicate with the heartbeat, which is a TRANSPORT ping that must NOT wait for the replay (the client's watchdog is ~27 s) - the split is the fix, and `_post_replay_started()` still returns `v3_responded` so the heartbeat is unaffected. THE REMAINING ONE IS NOT OURS: `GridTrackingComponentClientFacet_UpdatePhasing` fails at spawn-1ms while the message we send arrives **8 s after** the error, and the same single error appears in every session measured, including one with the state stream off - a client-side artifact of its own spawn sequence, bounded at one per session.

response_scheduling_is_request_correlate.what: MEASURED AND CHANGED, 2026-10-14. This CORRECTS `unrequested_client_facet_responses_were_dropped_or_deferred_20261013`: the decision rule was 'does the client have the facet?', measured by a survey of the live player entity's bound facets, and that is the wrong instrument for the question. The replay is ANOTHER CLIENT'S capture, so a typed response exists because some client sent the `*ServerFacet_*` request it answers; the question that decides whether to send it is whether OUR client sent that request. The old rule was wrong in both directions, and both are now fixed: `0x1067` VoiceChat `OnVoiceChatServiceRegistered` was DROPPED although the client does send `0x066B` `RegisterVoiceChatService` (now SENT), and `0x16A0` Inventories `OnQueryInventories` was SENT UNASKED although the client never sends `0x169D` (now DROPPED). `0x1B88` GlobalStorage `ReceiveStorageSearchItems` is still dropped but for the honest reason - the client never sends `0x1B7F` `RequestReplicateStorageSearchResults` - and `0x0CA4` EventNotification `SyncNotifications` is the ONLY remaining static drop (unsolicited, and its facet was measured absent). PAIRS, with how each was measured: `0x08E6` <- `0x09FC` (capture seq 59 -> 67), `0x1067` <- `0x066B` (seq 100 -> 101), `0x1096`/`0x1097` <- `0x1098` and `0x0635` (seq 110-114 -> 117/118, the ALC reply), `0x1033` <- the unnamed phasing family `0x101D/0x101E/0x102E/0x102F/0x192C` (seq 94-97 -> 98), `0x1B88` <- `0x1B7F`, `0x136A` <- `0x0CED`, `0x16A0` <- `0x169D` (the last three by family naming). The rule is: send a response once the client has sent its request, holding up to AZOTH_REPLAY_DEFER_TIMEOUT_S (default 20) then dropping with `event: replay-response-suppressed` and its reason; send an unsolicited response unless its facet was measured absent. VERIFIER: `scripts/request-response-map.py --check` re-derives the pairs from the capture and exits non-zero on a contradiction. COVERAGE: one `event: inbound-request-coverage` line per session splits the client's inbound types into `answerable_by_replay` and `no_replay_response` - a report, not a verdict, because many ServerFacet messages are setters answered by replicated state. NAMING DISCREPANCY RECORDED, NOT RESOLVED AWAY: the client reports `GridTrackingComponentClientFacet_UpdatePhasing` for the response we send as wire `0x1033`, while the wire-name registry pairs that NAME with wire 930, which the capture does not contain; the client's own error is the authority for what it received, so the table keeps `0x1033`. LIMIT: the acceptance measurement is still the previous policy's 29 -> 3 -> 1 dispatch errors per session; confirming that `0x1067` is accepted and `0x16A0` is no longer missed requires a live session, which was not run here. VERIFIED LIVE, TWICE, 2026-10-14. Both sessions held 32 responses and decided them IDENTICALLY: sent 0x08E6 (client sent 0x09FC), 0x1033 (0x101E/0x102E/0x102F/0x192C), 0x1067 (0x066B), 0x1096 and 0x1097 (0x0635/0x1098); suppressed 23x 0x1B88 (request-not-seen, 0x1B7F never sent), 2x 0x16A0 (request-not-seen, 0x169D never sent), 1x 0x136A (request-not-seen, 0x0CED never sent) and 1x 0x0CA4 (facet-absent). The client logged EXACTLY ONE RMIDispatch error in each run, GridTracking at spawn-3ms, the known artifact - and CRUCIALLY NO VoiceChat error although 0x1067 is now sent (so the reversal is accepted) and NO error for 0x16A0 although it is now suppressed (so the unasked message was never needed). Regressions clear in the same runs: movement 0.000 u baseline / 23.270 u under W, path 23.303 u; `Time since last response` 717/431/98 ms across three samples ~10 s apart; 26 slice lines both times; 0 errors, 0 transportError, 0 timeouts after spawn. RUN SEPARATELY: the first session's client died at 11 min 46 s with WER BEX64 frida-agent.dll_unloaded 0x9c7e0 P9=8, the documented execute-after-unload race caused by the measurement probe (which detached 8 min 48 s earlier), NOT by this change - frida-player-position.py now ends through _paths.safe_shutdown(). The LIMIT is therefore duration, not scheduling: no soak is claimed.

ack_range_pinned_to_session_start_breaks.va: rep.py::ACK_WINDOW, ack_window_first, handle_app_data(ack_first=...), ct_acks_datagram, carrier_state_datagram; measured from a live session log with scripts/ack-audit.py
ack_range_pinned_to_session_start_breaks.what: MEASURED AND FIXED, 2026-10-14. THE CLIENT'S END-OF-SESSION RETRANSMIT STORM HAS A SERVER-SIDE CAUSE, and it is an addressing window, not load. The Carrier CT_ACKS is a CONTINUOUS range `[ack_first, ack_last]` carried in two 16-BIT fields, and `ack_first` was pinned to the session's first inbound envelope sequence (`inbound_first`), so the acknowledged range grew by exactly one per datagram for the whole session. A wrap-aware reader cannot disambiguate a continuous range that is half the space or wider, and the client's response to the ambiguity is NOT an error - it RETRANSMITS. THE ONSET IS EXACT, TO THE SECOND: last inbound envelope seq below the boundary = 32767 at 08:42:44; first at/above = 32768 at 08:42:44 (the ACK range was 32766 wide at that instant); first retransmitted client record = reliable seq 1836 at 08:42:45, while every record up to 1835 had been sent exactly once. From there the client re-sent every reliable record it produced: 140 174 inbound channel-0 records in 10 minutes carrying only **660 distinct sequences**, a retransmit factor of **212x**, against **1.2x** earlier in the same session. The same storm caught wire 3639 (3 133 records, 202 distinct, 15.5x). PowerShell/evidence that it is not load or transport: the server's outbound rate was CONSTANT all session (2 626/min across the onset), its ACK rate was constant (665/min), the ACK range it sent was correct at every instant, and its own outbound reliable-sequence stream had no gap (two reordered pairs, no missing value). The client's `OnLocalNetworkConnectionWarning` counter climbs from spawn+1s and then accelerates ~24x at the onset. FIX: `ack_window_first` returns a SLIDING window - `ack_last - (min(datagrams_seen, ACK_WINDOW) - 1)`, computed in 16-bit wrap space from a MONOTONIC datagram count so it stays correct past the 65536 wrap (a pinned range could not survive that either). Default ACK_WINDOW=16384: half the safe maximum, and still ~13 minutes of history at the measured ~21 inbound datagrams/s. `handle_app_data` takes the windowed value as `ack_first` and falls back to `inbound_first` when a caller does not supply one. VERIFY with `python scripts/ack-audit.py <log>`: it reports the widest CT_ACKS range, whether any reached 32768, the envelope crossing, and the per-type retransmit factor, and it EXITS 1 on the pre-fix log of this session (7 496 ACK ranges at/over the limit, first at 08:42:44 with first=2 last=32770). VERIFIED LIVE, one-variable A/B, both arms the same build/env/machine and probe-free. PRE-FIX (spawn 08:16:51): crossed 32768 at 08:42:44, widest CT_ACKS range 56210, 7496 ranges at/over the limit, wire 349 retransmit factor 64x (142 088 records / 2 212 distinct), wire 3639 15.5x, 682 OnLocalNetworkConnectionWarning in 34 minutes, session ended at 34 min 10 s. FIXED (spawn 09:39:07): crossed the same 32768 boundary at 10:05:05, widest range 16383, ZERO ranges at/over the limit, wire 349 factor 1.0x (3 767 records / 3 764 distinct), wire 3639 1.0x, **ZERO connection warnings in 1 h 3 min 7 s** with only 2 [ERROR] lines (the spawn-3 ms GridTracking artifact and one client-content CameraLock), 0 transportError, 0 timeouts. THE 16-BIT WRAP WAS ALSO COVERED, live and unplanned: that run carried 79 616 inbound datagrams so the envelope sequence wrapped past 65535, and the auditor seized the range at first=63234 last=14081 - still exactly 16383 wide, which is the case the count-based design exists for and which a pinned ack_first could not have survived. DURATION IS NOT CLAIMED AS SOLVED: 1 h 3 min against a 34 min 10 s pre-fix best is one run, the crash history has at least three signatures, and a 2-hour soak is still outstanding.

The server had NO inbound typed dispatcher: every typed request the client made was acknowledged at the transport level and then ignored, with nothing in any log saying so (measured 19 requests in a short session, 29 in a richer one). THE REQUEST SHAPE IS NOW MEASURED, NOT GUESSED: every client->server typed request is `[u32 crc32][u32 len][16-byte facet target][00 01][prefix-varint type][params]`, so after the type marker the **first 16 bytes are the target facet's local id** - exactly the address a reply needs. `inbound-request-shape` records each known request's target and param length once per session, so the wire layout of a request is in the log next to its name. Measured shapes: 0x9d3 PlayerSettings ReceiveSettings (48B, target d1a94ccc870660b0bf85314bbc4a951a, 4 params), 0x9fc Contracts LookupContractsByParticipant (102B, target 4c0c0ed6478a69dabf85314bbc4a951a, 58 params), 0xa95 Objectives SetObjectiveAutoPinning (81B, target 180f8d4e573697c6bf85314bbc4a951a, 37), 0x183 GlobalStorage SetReplicateStorage (60B, target e2640b7ce5408036bf85314bbc4a951a, 16), 0x5b2 Objectives UpdateTrackedObjectives (45B, target 180f8d4e573697c6bf85314bbc4a951a, 1), 0x1098 Time SyncToClient (44B, target 93a3e477cb5fd51ebf85314bbc4a951a, 0). TWO CAPABILITIES THE REPLAY COULD NOT PROVIDE. (1) IT LEARNS THE TIME FACET'S ADDRESS FROM THE CLIENT ITSELF: 0x1098 carries 93a3e477cb5fd51ebf85314bbc4a951a and the captured 0x1096 body carries the same value as its own target, so the 0x1096/0x1097 reply is now addressed from the client's own request - verified by ALL 151 live `input-response` events reporting `target_source: client-request` - instead of from the capture or from `frida-facet-target-id.py` publishing an id to a file. `_read_input_response_target()` remains the fallback. (2) IT ANSWERS THE CONTRACTS REQUEST ONCE PER ASK: the client asked at 12:08:30 and 12:08:38 and BOTH got the captured 0x08E6 body (42 B; `inbound-answer n: 1` then `n: 2`), where the replay sends each captured body exactly once EVER. 0x08E6 therefore moved from the replay's request-gated defer set into DISPATCHER_OWNED_RESPONSES (`inbound-dispatcher-owned`, the held set went 32 -> 31), and the captured body is kept on the session as `contracts_response`; a target mismatch between the request and the captured body is LOGGED and the body is left alone rather than sent to a facet it was not addressed to. Pacing is counted, not silent (`inbound_answers_suppressed`). NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY: the five state-carrying requests (0x9d3 PlayerSettings, 0x5b2/0xa95 Objectives, 0x183 GlobalStorage) are decoded, counted and shape-logged but have NO authoritative effect; they remain in the coverage line's `no_replay_response`. Inventing a reply for a setter without evidence is what this repository forbids, so the next step is decoding each one's params and deciding per request what an authoritative effect requires. LEVERS: AZOTH_INBOUND_DISPATCH (default 1), AZOTH_INBOUND_ANSWER_INTERVAL_S (default 0.25), both readable from the session's own `config` event. CLIENT SIDE UNCHANGED AND CLEAN: 1 RMIDispatch error (the spawn-3 ms GridTracking artifact), 0 OnLocalNetworkConnectionWarning, 26 slice lines. The error count is unchanged across all four sessions since the deferral fix - the four TimeComponentClientFacet errors were removed by THAT fix two commits earlier, NOT by the dispatcher, and this session only confirms they did not come back. Regressions checked in the same session: movement 0.000 u baseline -> 22.998 u under W (path 23.028) -> 0.000 u after release; cable readout 498/265/266 ms; ACK widest range 6637 with 0 at/over the limit.

state_carrying_requests_have_no_reply_an.what: MEASURED NEGATIVE, 2026-10-14, and it REDIRECTS the authority work. The five state-carrying requests cannot be given an authoritative effect, for two independent reasons. (1) THE PROTOCOL HAS NO REPLY FOR THEM, checked per family in the name registry: `PlayerSettingsComponent` has exactly ONE message in the whole registry (the ServerFacet request `0x9d3`); `ObjectivesComponent`'s only client facets are `OnObjectiveWarning` (0xd6b), `OnMilestoneCorrection` (0xefc), `SetObjectiveInstanceDisabled` (0x1634) and a debug one - none is a 'here is your state' reply; `GlobalStorage`'s client facets are all storage-search results behind `0x1b7f`, which the client never sends. (2) THE ONE FAMILY THAT DOES HAVE A REPLY IS IGNORED BY THE CLIENT. Measured with a new instrument (`frida-game-time.py`, which runs the client's own `lc_getTime` console command and reads the printed `Current Container Time: h:m:s; t = ...; CryTime: h:m; DayPhase: ...` through the same printer `nw_getPlayerPosition` uses), across four fresh sessions: with the time sync sent, with it NOT sent at all, and with the `0x1097` payload forced to 0 and to 3, the client's clock advanced at **12.2x real time in every condition** and `DayPhase` displayed **`day` in every condition**. The forced value was confirmed ON THE WIRE (`...00000003` outbound, 241 logged override events) before concluding, so the client received it and still showed `day`. The client's clock and day phase are computed LOCALLY. (3) BYTE-IDENTICAL REPEATS ARE NOT A REQUEST FOR AN ANSWER: `0xa95` SetObjectiveAutoPinning is sent **17 times inside two seconds, up to 8 copies in a SINGLE datagram**, always with identical parameters, and `0x446` 15 times - the client's queue flushing duplicates, and the registry confirms no reply exists for either. REQUEST SHAPES measured: `0x9d3` 4B params `000097c9` (not a float, not a plausible int); `0x5b2` 1B `00` or 49B (three 16-byte session-scoped ids + `01`); `0xa95` 37B = `24` + 36 `00`/`01` bytes (a 36-flag bitfield, the `24`=36 being the remaining count); `0x183` 16B = 8-byte session id + 8 zeros; `0x1098` 0B (the request IS the message). The ids inside `0x5b2`/`0x183` appear neither as raw bytes nor as dashed strings in NewWorld.exe, so they are session-scoped and cannot be resolved statically. THE REDIRECT, WHICH IS THE ACTUAL RESULT: the one thing ever measured to make the client APPLY server data is REPLICATED STATE - the player moves while the record-1 `0x08` bundles flow and stops when they do not - while every typed reply tried so far has no target, no consumer, or no effect. So an authoritative effect must be expressed as replicated state, and the first one to build is a change to what the `0x08` bundles carry. That makes the ROADMAP item 4 Rust trigger concrete: the first state bundle the server composes itself. SIDE FINDING, also acted on: the request->facet topology is PER-FACET AND STABLE (all three Objectives requests carry the same 16-byte target `180f8d4e573697c6...`, both Mount requests `16009918b041c1f9...`, the Player-family `9e921a154971f6b7...`), which is why the dispatcher's target-learning generalises beyond the time facet. THE FAILED LEVER WAS REMOVED: AZOTH_DAY_PHASE_OVERRIDE, its helper and its three unit tests were deleted once the experiment came back negative, so `rep.py` is byte-identical to its committed state - a failed alternative does not stay in the runtime.

The .rdata descriptor form is `<Name>�<pad>�<GUID1>�<GUID2>` for some types - one name followed by TWO GUIDs - and the adjacency rule then names both, because the nearest preceding printable run for GUID2 is still GUID1's name. state_bundle_fragment_grammar_derived_fr.what: MEASURED, 2026-10-14, and it RESOLVES the open question in bundle.py's own docstring and the contradiction with atlas entry 635. THE FRAGMENT GRAMMAR IS `[varint key][varint type_index][payload]` WITH NO LENGTH FIELD - the payload length is implied by the type. Derived from the client, not guessed: a probe hooks the record reader, the fragment reader and the shared prefix-varint reader and logs each fragment's offset from the record start plus every varint read inside it. The same run reproduced the local-player record's nine boundaries 21 times, and the (key, type) pair it reported per fragment matches an independent byte-level parse of the payload, so two methods agree. THE LOCAL-PLAYER METADATA RECORD (record_id 1) AND ITS NINE FRAGMENTS, in payload-offset order: (2,58,key 55,type 4176), (60,3895,19,3133), (3955,340,73,5606), (4295,6,9,3935), (4301,197,72,5485), (4498,837,74,5691), (5335,51,16,11), (5386,1739,22,3857), (7125,29,44,4236). Boundaries cannot be COMPUTED from the bytes (no length field), so they are recorded protocol data in research/derived/state-bundle-fragments.json. ATLAS ENTRY 635 IS WRONG about the fragment layout (`[varint key][varint type][3 bytes 01 00 00][varint payload_length][payload]`): that model fails immediately on the record-1 bundle - it reads fragment 0's key as 55, its type as 4176 and then a length of 11563 from a 7154-byte payload. It was accepted because 'consumes the body exactly' cannot discriminate against an opaque remainder, which is the very trap bundle.py's docstring warns about. The 3-byte `01 00 00` it records is real BYTES but they are the START of a fragment payload, not a per-fragment prefix. TOOL NOTE: the probe was converted from a bare `session.detach()` to `_paths.safe_shutdown()` - the bare detach is the measured cause of an execute-after-unload client crash that has twice been misread as a client bug - and it now captures the record reader's out_u16 so a fragment event names its record.

state_bundle_can_be_composed_from_fragme.what: BUILT AND VERIFIED LIVE, 2026-10-14, TWO RUNS. The server can now COMPOSE a type-0x08 state bundle from its fragments instead of forwarding a captured body, and the client parses and applies it. This is the direction the previous negative result pointed at: the one thing ever measured to make the client APPLY server data is replicated state, and the state bundle is now something the server builds. RUN A, authoritative on, no override: **487 recompositions, all 487 `identical: true`, 0 failures** - the identity is asserted on EVERY send, so enabling the path cannot change behaviour by accident, and a layout that stopped matching the build logs `state-authoritative-failed` instead of sending something wrong. RUN B, `AZOTH_STATE_OVERRIDE=key=16,off=8,hex=010203`: **672 sends, all `override_applied`**, logged transition `override_from: 0975bf` -> `override_to: 010203`, **0 failures, 0 `Failed to unmarshal`, 0 ValidationError**, 1 client error (the known spawn-3 ms GridTracking artifact), and the world rendering normally - so the client parses and applies a bundle whose bytes WE composed. WHY key=16 WAS CHOSEN: across the four captured copies of the record-1 bundle the payloads are identical EXCEPT for exactly three bytes at payload offsets 5345-5347, and both values differ per copy (0975bf vs 0aa7c2); those bytes fall inside fragment key 16 (type 11, 49-byte payload), making it the only field the capture itself proves is live state. A test asserts that remains true, so the constant cannot drift silently. REGRESSIONS CLEAR in run A (probe-free for the cable): movement 0.000 u baseline -> **27.142 u** with W held 5 s (path 27.142 = straight) -> 0.000 u after release; the client's own cable readout 67/330/433 ms across three samples ~10 s apart; 0 transportError, 0 State(InGame) is timeout, 0 Disconnected from REP. NOT CLAIMED: the overridden field's MEANING is undecoded - nothing observable changed between run A and run B under 010203, so it is either cosmetic state or that value is inert; the path composes ONE record from ONE record's fragments while everything else in the stream is still forwarded verbatim; and AZOTH_STATE_AUTHORITATIVE defaults to 0, so the path is proven but not adopted. NEXT STEP THIS OPENS: make the composed bundle carry a field whose effect IS measurable - the position, which the client reads back through its own accessor (`nw_getPlayerPosition`). Locate the field in the record-1 fragments first; do not guess an offset into a 7154-byte payload.

server_owns_the_player_position_measured.what: MEASURED AND VERIFIED LIVE, 2026-10-14. **THE SERVER OWNS THE PLAYER'S POSITION.** This is the first authoritative EFFECT in the project - not 'we composed bytes the client accepted' but 'we decided where the player is and it went there'. WHERE THE POSITION ACTUALLY LIVED, AND WHY IT NEVER MOVED: it is NOT in the 7154-byte record-1 bundles the state stream sends; it is in the **46393-byte** record-1 bundles - the SPAWN record, 48 fragments, replay seq 0x2a..0x6c - which sit BELOW the stream's MIN_SEQ floor of 0x94, so the replay sends them once and the stream never does. That is the entire reason the position stayed anchored at the capture's value for the whole history of this project. FOUND BY VALUE, NOT BY A GUESSED OFFSET: x 9343.6416015625 and y 2786.732666015625 sit at payload offsets 38332/38336 as big-endian float32, byte-exact against the position the client's own accessor had always reported. **z IS NOT IN THE PAYLOAD** - searched f32/f64 both endians and scaled i16/i32/i64 at x1/x10/x100/x1000/x1024, zero hits - so the wire carries a 2D position. THE MEASUREMENT: AZOTH_STATE_POSITION=9353.7227,2766.0681 (a point the client itself had reported after walking, ~23 u from the capture's spawn). SERVER SIDE: 24 `state-position-override` events, each `replacements: 1`, on seq 0x2a/0x2b/0x2e/0x2f/0x30/0x33... - exactly the spawn bundles and nothing else, because the override is anchored on the measured capture value and fires only in a body that actually carries it. CLIENT SIDE, through its own accessor: reported position (9353.72265625, 2766.068115234375, 87.5379638671875) = **0.0000 u** from what the server wrote and **22.9925 u** from what the capture carried, so there is no ambiguity about which one it used. THE z QUESTION IS ANSWERED: z VARIES across the 199 samples (87.432 -> 87.611) while x and y sit exactly on our values, so the client derives the height and the server decides only where in the plane the player is. IT IS A STARTING POINT, NOT A FREEZE: with W held 5 s from there the player moved 14.005 u and stopped again after release (net 0.000 u over 120 samples). NOTHING REGRESSED: 1 RMIDispatch error (the known spawn-3 ms GridTracking artifact), 0 connection warnings, 0 Failed to unmarshal / ValidationError, 0 transportError/timeouts/REP disconnects, world rendered with 26 slice lines. NOT CLAIMED: one session and one injected value; the override writes x and y only (the client owns the height); and the position is applied AT SPAWN from a record the replay sends once, so this is authority over the starting point, not yet over the position over time. AZOTH_STATE_POSITION defaults to empty, so the capture's position is used unless it is set. A LAUNCHER DEFECT WAS FOUND ON THE WAY: the first attempt failed with `FAIL: window never appeared` and it was NOT the client - Windows PowerShell 5.1 on this machine loads Microsoft.PowerShell.Utility but does not expose Get-FileHash, which Start-NwPrivate.ps1 calls to record the client's source hash, so the launcher died with `The term 'Get-FileHash' is not recognized`. pwsh 7 is installed and the runbook already records that it, not 5.1, is the shell that script needs; az.py and scripts/private-run.py now prefer pwsh and fall back, so a machine without it behaves as before.

client_channel_one_carries_the_players_p.va: services/world/src/azoth_world/javelin/alc.py::split_container, read_position, read_claim, is_world_ready; scripts/alc-position.py; wire type 0x635 (1589) ActionListComponentServerFacet_ReceiveInputFromClient, channel 1
client_channel_one_carries_the_players_p.what:
MEASURED 2026-10-18 over 213,202 captured channel-1 records (services/world/rep_traffic.jsonl, the 2026-10-14 sessions). **The client's own input stream DOES carry the player's position, and the server can read it.** This corrects the older record that the channel-1 body was 'byte identical across 3038 records' with 'no position, no orientation, no velocity': that measurement was of the SHORT body shape (92-154 bytes), which is the pre-spawn form. Once the player entity exists the body grows and carries a position. CONTAINER: [u32 BE crc32][u32 BE len][16-byte target][00 01][prefix-varint type][body]. The target is the local player's actor id (1a954abc4b3185bfbe37c3d8592618e0). The type is **0x635 = 1589, NOT 0xC35**: `b5 18` is a PREFIX varint, so the low six bits of the leading byte carry data and the value is (0x18 << 6) | 0x35 = 1589. Reading it as LEB128 gives 3125 and then rejects every real record; this was caught by a test, not by inspection. The body starts at payload offset 28. POSITION: two consecutive big-endian float32. It is NOT at a fixed offset - the body is a variable-length sequence, so the block sits at body offset 91 in the dominant form and at 93, 92, 101, 112 in others (measured distribution). What IS stable is the four bytes preceding it, `3d 4c cc cd` = the float32 0.05, with the pair at marker+12. Over the 213,202 records: 197,810 carry a position, 15,392 do not (pre-load bodies), and **0** carry more than one marker, so the locator is unambiguous. A hard-coded offset of 103 reads the wrong bytes on the 11,144 records whose block sits at 93. Verified with scripts/alc-position.py and 15 tests in services/world/tests/test_alc.py whose fixtures are real captured payloads.

CORRECTION 2026-10-18 (later, and it is a significant one): **the `x,y` in the channel-1 body is NOT a live position feed.** It is a spawn/reference anchor that changes only on teleport or respawn. MEASURED with the client's own position accessor polled at 20 Hz while the player walked: the accessor recorded a real 23 u walk (9343.64,2786.73) -> (9353.72,2766.06) over 5 s, while the channel-1 claim stayed at (9341.44,2790.11) with **0 changes across 1050 samples** in the same minute. Across 20:5x-21:0x there were **2 distinct claim values and 1 change**, a 243 u respawn jump. The earlier note that '197810 records carry a position' is true about the FIELD but not about its meaning: the field is present and readable, and it does not track locomotion. See `the_channel_one_position_is_a_spawn_anchor_not_a_live_feed_20261018`.

reference_offset_is_an_instrument_proper.what: MEASURED 2026-10-18, and it is the reason a desync threshold could not be tightened. **The position on the wire is NOT the same quantity the client's own nw_getPlayerPosition accessor reports.** Paired sample by sample with the accessor while the player stood still, the wire claim sits 2.0-4.0 u away, and the offset is PER SESSION: (-2.196,+3.370) |d|=4.022, (-1.183,+1.847) |d|=2.193, (-2.200,+3.378) |d|=4.031, (-2.260,+3.202) |d|=3.919, (-0.313,-0.475) |d|=0.569, (+0.502,-3.991) |d|=4.023. Within a session it is CONSTANT - the residual is 0.0000 u in two of them and under 0.26 u in three more - so the reader is precise and the offset is a real constant of that session, not noise. The one session with residual 3.49 u is the one where the client's reported position was changing, i.e. the calibration is correctly flagged untrustworthy. THE DESIGN CONSEQUENCE, which is the actual result: this offset must be kept OUT of the desync path. Treating it as desync means reporting a 2-4 u error for a perfectly in-sync player, and it is why a threshold below that band produces permanent false positives. DesyncTracker therefore compares the client's claim against the SERVER's own authoritative position - the same quantity in the same frame of reference, needing no offset at all - and ReferenceOffset exists only to validate the instrument from paired probe samples and to translate a claim when a probe is the only witness. Negative result also recorded: the client's exact accessor position bytes appear in **0 of 213,202** channel-1 payloads in any encoding tried (f32/f64 both endians, scaled i16/i32/i64 at x1/x10/x100/x1000/x1024), so the wire value is a different point in the client's pipeline, not a rounded copy of the rendered position.

load_signal_is_the_input_body_growing_20.what: MEASURED 2026-10-18 over 12 recorded sessions in services/world/rep_traffic.jsonl. **There is a real 'the player is in the world' signal, and it arrives 8-14 s after the first channel-1 record, not at 60 s.** The client's input body grows 93 -> 108 -> 123 -> 138 -> 153 -> 154 bytes and only carries a position once it crosses roughly 280 bytes (payload 308). The first position-bearing record arrived at t+11, +10, +9, +8, +9, +9, +14, +12, +11 and +8 s in ten sessions. One session (2026-10-14 18:50:56Z) never grew past 154 bytes and produced NO position in 400 records - a failed load, which the gate correctly reports as 'never ready' instead of letting the server validate a stream that carries no claim. So a fixed 60 s grace period is both too slow, because it blinds the server for 45-50 s of a window in which the player is already controllable, and uninformative, because it cannot distinguish a loaded session from a failed one. The gate should key on the position marker appearing, with the timeout as a diagnostic rather than as the rule.
