the_slice_job_does_not_implement_the_int.what: MEASURED 2026-10-19, in RUNTIME, and it is the definitive answer to why the Transform gate never registers. Probe `frida-gate-qi` called the two TLS-cached GUID getters and then called the slice job's own QueryInterface directly, so nothing here is inferred from disassembly. THE QUERYINTERFACE. The gate does `job->vtable[+0x20](job, guid)`; all 30 slice jobs share ONE vtable (RVA 0x7feaca8) and its `+0x20` slot is RVA 0x1445390, which is a REAL QueryInterface: it compares the requested GUID against two, returns `this` on a match, and returns 0 otherwise. THE THREE CALLS, on job 0x2067b611c00: `83482f97-84da-4fd4-bf9e-7fe34c8e091f` -> **null** (this is the one the gate asks for); `ed75fe05-9196-4f69-a3e5-1bdf5ff034cf` -> `0x2067b611c00` (accepted); `b18d903b-7fad-4a53-918a-3967b3198224` -> `0x2067b611c00` (accepted). So the QueryInterface WORKS and the gate's null is simply 'this object does not implement that interface'. The second accepted GUID resolves in the AZ type registry to **`ReflectContext`**; the other two have no name in the registry, which only names 750 of the 7052 type-table entries. CONSEQUENCE, and it closes a line of investigation: the fix is NOT to reach the gate (it runs 30 times), NOT to patch the lookup's answer (tried: 26 warnings -> 0 but 26 `The slice has more than one root` errors and an APPCRASH in NewWorld.exe), and NOT an alignment artefact in a static vtable read. The slice job genuinely does not implement `{83482F97-...}`, so `FUN_141582430` - the only inserter of GameTransformComponent into the clone's class map - is unreachable through this path in this build. WHERE THAT LEAVES THE ENTITY WORK: a correct fix must supply the class-map entry by the same route the client's own spawn record uses for the local player (which DOES get a Transform - the player is visible), rather than by answering this interface or by handing back a default-constructed component. The asymmetry to exploit is measured and concrete: the local player renders and remote entities do not, both through the same slice asset, so the difference is in what seeds the map for the player's path, and that is the next thing to find.

The first session measured 31 / 1 / 1 with a narrower range set; the ratio is the same and the player count is higher because more of the heap was covered. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE STORY: an actor the client fully knows is referenced **31 times** (entity table, components, slice instances, indices); an actor that is only registered is referenced **once**. METHOD NOTE for anyone reusing this scan: the budget matters more than the pattern. the_26_transform_warnings_are_a_fixed_pr.what: MEASURED 2026-10-19, and it changes the status of the Transform gap from 'a symptom of our replay' to 'a fixed property of this client build'. The count of `Slice: Couldn't get Transform component on the slice!` for `slices/remoteplayer.dynamicslice` is **exactly 26 in EVERY session on record**, checked across twelve retained Game.log files: prev4, prev5, qi, returnsite, retval0, retvalname, run1h24m, seqgate, slot3, soak37, withnpc - and **stale-20261010, which is from a DIFFERENT DAY**. THE GATE COUNT CORROBORATES IT: `FUN_141763b70` runs **30 times** in a session, and 26 of those lookups come back null. So the client instantiates a FIXED set of remote-player slices, and a fixed subset of them fails to get a Transform. WHY THIS IS THE USEFUL REFRAMING: the missing body is NOT caused by the record the server sends. It is a structural condition of this build's slice path, present since at least 2026-10-10, which is why every attempt to fix it by changing the record (payload shape, flag, slot, seq, actor id) failed identically and why the one attempt that bypassed it broke the slice's root and crashed. WHAT IT IMPLIES FOR THE ROADMAP: item 1 ('a NEW actor') and item 2 ('second player') both depend on remote-player slices being placeable, and that is now measured to be broken for the CAPTURED actors too - not just for one the server creates. So the honest order is: make ONE remote-player slice placeable (by making the client's own registration run), and only then talk about creating actors. Its position pair (9345.4609, 2781.2595) is carried by TWO bundles, measured: `0x77` (record 29, payload offset 238) and `0xa1` (record 29, payload offset 238). `0x77` is BELOW the state stream's floor of 0x94, so the REPLAY sends it once and the stream never does - which means the previous call site, gated on `msg.seq == MOVE_ACTOR_SEQ`, only ever patched the STREAM copy and left the creation bundle at the capture's position. That is the same defect the structure experiment already paid for, and it is now fixed (see `the_actor_move_was_gated_on_the_source_seq_and_missed_the_creation_bundle_20261020`). With the by-value rewrite the log shows the write on `0x77` (the replay) and on `0xa1` (the stream), the client accepted everything (0 `Failed to unmarshal`, 0 `ValidationError`, 0 `more than one root`, 26 Transform warnings = the fixed baseline), and NO BODY APPEARS at 5.8 u from the player. ARM 2 - SARADNAX (seq 0x97, record 94). Its slice instance is at payload 291, `<remoteplayer.dynamicslice GUID><00 00 00 02><actor 8e4972ff...>`, and the 8 bytes that follow the actor id are `18b03301040001a0` - i.e. the position slot that holds a real f32 pair in record 29 (payload 684, after the actor at 662) holds 0.0 here. Moving one requires first identifying, from the client, which actor id the client actually bound to a rendered slice and reading THAT entity's transform - which is exactly the actor/entity census (FUN_146801040, manager at this+0x110, probes frida-entity-table.py / frida-actor-presence.py) that the roadmap already names as the next instrument. Verified live: the log shows `actor-moved` on `seq 0x77` (the replay) and on `seq 0xa1` (the stream) in the same session. A test pins both halves - that the call site is not gated on the source seq, and that exactly two captured bundles carry the pair with the smaller one below the stream floor. THE LAYOUT: the world position is three floats at Transform **+0x14c (x), +0x15c (y), +0x16c (z)** - STRIDE 0x10, NOT a contiguous 12-byte (x,y,z) triple. (2) reading those same three offsets on the twelve remote entities reproduces the positions the capture declares, 0.5-2.3 u apart (rid29, rid30, rid60, rid79, rid87, rid88, rid89, rid90, rid91, rid92, rid93, rid94 - all matched), and on the local player it reproduces exactly the value the accessor reports, (9343.6416, 2786.7327, 87.538). prefix_varint_reader_1460.what: The prefix-varint reader on the installed 1.460 build. Shape: read one byte; if it is below 0x80 the value is that byte; below 0xc0 take 1 more byte and use shift 6 with mask 0x3f; below 0xe0 take 2 more and use shift 5 with mask 0x1f; below 0xf0 take 3 more and use shift 4; otherwise 4 more. Continuation bytes are read little-endian and ORed above the first byte's low bits, and the cursor at state+0x10 is bounds-checked against state+0x8 before each read.

fragment_payload_is_delta_20261026.what:
MEASURED 2026-10-26. State-bundle FRAGMENT PAYLOADS ARE NOT FIXED-LAYOUT STRUCTS. They are baseline/delta blobs: the spawn record is the baseline carrying every field, and later records carry only what changed. Three independent signals.

(1) THE UPDATE OMITS A FIELD THE BASELINE CARRIES. Type 11 (ALCReplicatedState) has an 87-byte body at spawn payload 38310..38397, with the authoritative x/y at payload +20 as f32be (9343.6416015625, 2786.732666015625). The same key (16) and type (11) at payload offset 5335 of the 9-fragment record does NOT contain that pair anywhere in its 7,153 bytes: searched f32be pair, f32le pair, f32be/f32le each component alone, all zero hits, while the spawn's 46,393 bytes match at 38332 exactly. A present-but-stale field would still match; absence cannot be a stale fixed offset.

(2) THE CLIENT'S OWN READS MOVE, as supporting evidence only. The nested prefix-varint reads inside the same fragment type sit at offsets 29, 32, 34, 37, 38, 41 in one instance and 33, 36, 38, 41, 43, 46 in another, with the same VALUES (31, 1081) at the shifted offsets (fragment-grammar.jsonl, varints recorded by the client's own reader FUN_14087b5c0). A variable-length field ahead of them would also shift them, so this rules out a flat fixed struct but does not by itself establish delta encoding. Signal (1) carries the argument alone: absent is not stale.

(3) THE MECHANISM IS IN THIS BUILD. The client registers `statereplication-enable-hub-delta-compression` and `asc-enable-fragment-sharing` among the 452 javelin-server.* cvars, so delta compression is a supported feature here rather than an inference drawn from the bytes.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT GIVE: the delta format itself. The field mask, the present-field list and the reference state a delta applies against are all unmeasured, and three instances are not enough to recover them. Do not guess them.

CONSEQUENCE FOR RUNG 17: with no fixed offset to patch, 'find what the captured spawn does not supply' is the wrong question for a record whose fields are conditional. The right question is whether the client rejects the record or accepts it and then waits for something else, which needs a handler hook, not more byte reading.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RUST PORT: a server that ECHOES captured bytes satisfies this format for free, because it never encodes a delta. A server that AUTHORS state (spawning a second entity, moving one, setting a component) must produce deltas against the reference state the client holds, and that encoder is the real work item. It is blocked by the format, not by naming.

CORRECTION OF MY OWN METHOD NOTE: an earlier step this session matched the byte pattern `10 0b` inside other records (offsets 298, 460, 630) and treated those as type-11 fragment headers. Only 5335 and 38310 are backed by a live measurement of a fragment header; the others were two-byte pattern hits that could equally be data, and no conclusion here rests on them.

naming_tiebreaker_table_row_20261026.what:
MEASURED 2026-10-26. The 796 'ambiguous' wire types (23% of the 3,390 the hook naming pass reported) were a TOOL DEFECT, not a client property.

DIAGNOSIS. A registration table is a run of 48-byte ROWS. Each row starts with the address of the lambda that owns it and carries that row's type-descriptor thunk at +0x08. `resolve` read eight consecutive qwords from the TABLE BASE and treated each as a descriptor of the type being named, so the answer included the NEXT row's type as well. The giveaway was the shape of the ambiguity: 782 of the 796 rows held exactly two names, and they were consistently 'slot 1' and 'slot 7' = +0x08 and +0x08+48. A genuine many-to-one mapping would not land on two fixed offsets; one row plus its neighbour would.

FIX. entry_descriptor(record_va, lambda_va) walks rows and returns the descriptor of the ONE row whose first qword equals that lambda. Applied as a TIE-BREAKER: if it yields exactly one name the row wins, otherwise the slot scan is used unchanged, so the rule can only narrow a candidate set and never remove a name that the slot scan had alone.

EVIDENCE, all on 30fe6461: (a) all 796 ambiguous types return exactly one name; (b) on the 2,594 previously-unambiguous types it agrees 2,576 times, returns nothing 18 times, and CONTRADICTS ZERO; (c) on the 7 replay types whose names are known independently it is correct 7/7. (c) is why this is a measurement, and 0x663 is inside it: the tie-breaker returns LevelInfoChangedMsg alone where the slot scan also offered 'State', and LevelInfoChangedMsg is proven by decompiling FUN_146447ac0, independently of the naming tool.

THE 18 MISSES ARE WHY IT IS NOT A REPLACEMENT. Example: 0x96 UnregisterProxyMsg, whose owning row's descriptor thunk is not the `lea rax,[rip]; ret` shape thunk_target expects, so entry_descriptor finds the row but the descriptor does not resolve. Those fall back. Uniqueness alone is trivially faked by choosing a wrong-but-consistent row, which is why the ground-truth set and the never-drop test exist (reverse/tools/tests/test_message_naming.py, 5 tests).

SCOPE LIMIT: this improves TYPE names only. It says nothing about field layouts, and a named type still has an unmeasured body.

CAVEAT FOUND AFTER THE FIX, and it must not be read past: the type table holds TRAIT registrations as well as message ones, and the mangled name says which -- InstallRegistrationHook<VPersistenceRestoreListenerTrait@...> takes a trait as its template argument, InstallRegistrationHook<VLevelInfoChangedMsg@...> takes a message. So the tie-breaker can return a name ending in 'Trait' for a wire number: 0x19 -> PersistenceRestoreListenerTrait, where the slot scan offered AckMovementMsg. Both are real table entries; WHICH ONE OWNS THAT GUID IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and the ground-truth set of 7 contains no such case, so the 7/7 result says nothing about it. A row whose answer ends in 'Trait' should be read as 'a trait registration, or the slot scan's candidate' and not as a decision. This is the honest boundary of the 796 result: uniqueness is measured for all 796, correctness is measured for 7.

FULL SWEEP REGENERATED 2026-10-26 (31m55s, research/derived/message-names.json), and the headline is stability, not size: 3,390 named / 97 no-hook-record / 3,565 no-guid-string -- the SAME counts as the defective pass, so no name was invented or lost. Every named row now holds exactly ONE name (all 3,390), where 796 held two or more. resolution: 3,372 entry-match, 18 slot-scan. Against the previous artifact: 2,594 previously-unambiguous rows compared, ZERO name changes, zero lost, zero gained -- the fix did not rewrite a single settled answer. Of the 796 newly single-name rows, 21 now land on a name ending in 'Trait' (85 such rows table-wide, the other 64 already were), which is the caveat below, not a new failure.

delta_format_measured_20261026.va: 0x146af38c0 (fragment reader), 0x142a44650 (ALC payload reader), 0x142a3f120 (ALC payload writer), 0x142a28350 (delta decompressor), 0x1461ae2a0 (type-index -> id table)
delta_format_measured_20261026.what:
MEASURED 2026-10-26 by decompiling the fragment READER and, independently, the fragment WRITER. This replaces the earlier 'the delta format is unmeasured' state.

Q1 -- WHY A FRAGMENT HAS NO LENGTH FIELD. `0x146af38c0` reads the key varint, the type-index varint, resolves the type object, then hands the live stream to that object's VIRTUAL SLOT +0x90 and lets the type consume what it consumes. The consumed count is computed AFTERWARDS as position_after - position_before and passed only to FUN_146a64be0 / FUN_146a64170, which are log helpers. So the boundaries are not derivable from the bytes because the format does not encode them; the schema implies the length. The record reader 0x146af3650 loops a SINGLE-BYTE count. Therefore record := varint record_id | u8 fragment_count | fragment*, and fragment := varint key | varint type_index | payload.

Q2 -- FIELD PRESENCE IS THE DELTA. ALCReplicatedState (type id 01B0664B-3AB6-44A6-87E3-8C69D40E0365, index 11, vtable 0x148100b10; +0x90 = 0x142a44650) reads: u8 top_mask (raw byte, not a varint), then per set bit of top_mask a varint64 field_mask masked to 54 bits (0x3fffffffffffff), then the present fields in ascending bit order each through its own vtable+0x30 codec. Three independent numbers agree on 54: each group is 0x3b0 bytes = 54 x 0x10 descriptor slots + 0x50 header; the mask constant is 2^54-1; the loop bound computes 0x360>>4 = 54.

THE WRITER IS THE CHECK THAT MAKES IT MEASURED. +0x88 = 0x142a3f120 collects presence bits, writes the body, seeks back to the payload start (+0x48), writes the single mask byte (+0x40), seeks to end (+0x38). The mask is a BACK-PATCH because presence is not known until every predicate has run. Reader and writer deriving the same constant from opposite directions is what lifts this from inference to measurement. bit set <=> field on the wire; an unset field is ABSENT, not stale. That is the mechanism behind the missing position pair.

Q3 -- THE TYPE INDEX IS A REGISTRY. 0x1461ae2a0 maps the varint index to a 16-byte type id through a flat table at registry+0x40, stride 0x10, bounds-checked against registry+0x48; INDEX 0 IS THE ESCAPE that carries the 16 id bytes inline. 0x1461ae3f0 then calls 0x146166220, a hash map keyed by that id: node +0x10/+0x18 are the key halves, +0x20 is the type object. Missing key returns 0 and the fragment fails.

Q4 -- THE REFERENCE STATE IS THE ABSOLUTE PORTION, IN THE SAME FIELD. ALC carries each quantity twice with separate presence bits: worldPosRel (bit 10) / worldPosAbs (bit 26), idRel (0) / idAbs (24), timeOffsetRel (1) / timeOffsetAbs (25). The value transform is vtable +0x78 = 0x142a3dd60, a two-line trampoline into 0x142a28350: value = *(float*)(member+0x10) + dequantize(byte at member+0x60, scale at +0x88), likewise +0x14/+0x61 and +0x18/+0x62. The same function's failure branch carries the client's own contract statement from .rdata 0x1480ffab0: 'Absolute portion in delta compression wasn't set! We can't calculate the value.', with reflection key 'DeltaCompression' at 0x1480ffb00. A delta with no absolute base is therefore FATAL rather than stale -- the client refuses to compute and says so.

INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION ACROSS TYPES. In fragment-grammar.jsonl (300 fragments, many types) the first payload varint, measured from the end of the type-index varint, sits at offsets 2, 3, 4, 10, 19, 23, 27, 31 -- 0 and 1 NEVER occur and 2 is the floor, which is exactly one mask byte + one field-mask varint. rung17_log_strings_have_no_xref_20261026.what:
TWO MEASURED NEGATIVES, 2026-10-26, both re-checked by the parent against the binary. Kept because they close routes that would otherwise be tried again.

(1) THE RUNG-17 LOG STRINGS HAVE NO REFERENCE IN THE IMAGE. 'skipping ReceiveStateBundle' at 0x148500708, 'clientContext == nullptr' at 0x14850073e and 'player spawn succeeds' at 0x1484ffeff each have ZERO rip-relative lea xrefs (exhaustive scan over all four REX prefixes with a ModRM mod=00 rm=101 check), no imm64 reference and no pointer-table entry. Zero is surprising for strings that demonstrably reach the client's own log, and it means the logging call site cannot be found by scanning for the string address. Whatever reads them does not load the address the way a normal lea does.

(2) THE TWO VERIFIED HANDLERS DID NOT FIRE. A probe hooked twelve slots of processor vtable 0x148590ab8 plus the two handlers verified on this build, 0x146455ec0 (0x65c) and 0x146447ac0 (0x663). 1015 calls landed on other slots of the same vtable (0x14029e840 took 1001, 0x1402a0100 took 14) while BOTH verified handlers took 0.

THE TRAP, recorded because it was a real error and not a subtlety. That second negative was first read as 'the atlas dispatch claim is wrong, vtable+0x20 is not the dispatch'. IT IS NOT WRONG: vtable 0x148590ab8 + 0x20 IS 0x14029f9f0, re-checked this session against the binary, and that same pointer fills 24 slots of the table. What the zero actually means is that THE RUN NEVER REACHED THE DISPATCH at all: in that run's Game.log, WaitingForSpawnPoint and WaitingForPlayerSpawn occur ZERO times and the log ends during CMS file loading -- the client never entered the world. A probe on a client stuck at a loading screen measures a live client doing nothing on the path of interest; 1015 calls elsewhere proves the hooks were live and proves nothing about dispatch.

THE RULE THIS YIELDS, worth more than either negative: BEFORE reading any live negative about a protocol path, confirm from the client's own log that the run REACHED that path. Hooks firing is evidence the probe works, never evidence that the client entered the state under test. Diagnostic that caught it: Game.log was 50 KB against 206 KB for the reference run at .azoth/logs/runs/run-20261026-1460-ladder/, and grep for the ladder states returned 0.
